**SInfoNiA — Strategic Information: New Directions and Applications** was awarded an ERC Advanced Grant in 2024 and is funded by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI).

SInfoNiA studies how information coordinates economic activity and shapes strategic interaction. It develops a theory of strategic types that describes information through its relevance to a given game, with applications to financial stability, robust economic predictions and social norms.

The research is organised into seven work packages:

- **WP1 — Strategic types:** develop a framework applicable to a broad range of games.
- **WP2 — Measuring and valuing information:** develop new ways to quantify information and assess its economic value.
- **WP3 — Connections with global games:** bring strategic types and global-games information structures into a unified framework.
- **WP4 — Algorithms:** develop computational methods that make the theory widely usable.
- **WP5 — Financial stability:** extend global-games analysis to new models of financial stability.
- **WP6 — Robustness:** examine how robust economic outcomes are, including in trade and financial networks.
- **WP7 — Information and incentive design:** jointly design information and incentives to achieve desirable outcomes, including interventions to change social norms and address gender inequality.

[ERC project description (CORDIS)](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101142530) · [Project website at CREST](https://crest.science/erc-grants/sinfonia/)

## Workshops

SInfoNiA funds workshops within the recurring [Paris Game Theory Festival](https://sites.google.com/view/parisgtfestival/), which brings together researchers in game theory, information and language at the Institut Henri Poincaré and Université Paris Panthéon-Assas.

### 2027 — forthcoming

- [3rd Paris Workshop on Game Theory and Information](https://sites.google.com/view/parisgtfestival/2027), 7–9 June, Institut Henri Poincaré.
- [5th Paris Workshop on Game Theory and Language](https://sites.google.com/view/parisgtfestival/2027/5th-language-workshop), 10–11 June, Université Paris Panthéon-Assas.

### 2026

- [2nd Paris Workshop on Game Theory and Information](https://sites.google.com/view/parisgtfestival/2026/program), 8–10 June, Institut Henri Poincaré.
- [4th Paris Workshop on Game Theory and Language](https://sites.google.com/view/parisgtfestival/2026/4th-language-workshop), 11–12 June, Université Paris Panthéon-Assas. This edition marked the fiftieth anniversary of “Agreeing to Disagree”, with Robert Aumann.

### 2025

- [Paris Workshop on Game Theory and Information](https://sites.google.com/view/parisgtfestival/2025/interactive-beliefs), 2–4 June, Institut Henri Poincaré.
- [3rd Paris Workshop on Game Theory and Language](https://sites.google.com/view/parisgtfestival/2025/3rd-language-workshop), 5–7 June, Université Paris Panthéon-Assas.
